summary: W. H. D. Rouse was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell. He was a fellow and later Lecturer in Sanskrit at Christ's College, Cambridge, and Headmaster of The Perse School (1902–1928).

W. H. R. Rivers studied medicine at St Bartholomew's and the University of London. Active in psychology and anthropology, he lectured at Cambridge (1893–1908), became a fellow of St John's College, and served as President of the Royal Anthropological Institute.

W. Haskell was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Dartmouth and Yale, completing doctoral work under William Dwight Whitney around 1874–1876, and served as a librarian at Yale University from 1875 to 1905.

W. Norman Brown was an Indologist and historian who studied at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield and Franklin Edgerton. He taught at Johns Hopkins, Government Sri Pratap Memorial Rajput College, and served as Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1926–1966).

W. Randolph Kloetzli works in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago in 1964 and lectured at American University, George Washington University, and Dartmouth College.

W. S. Karunatillake is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as Professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1997) and was Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard University in 1998.
W. W. Tarn was a historian of Central Asia and Iran. He was educated at Eton College and Trinity College, Cambridge, where he later served as a Fellow.

Wadigala Samitharathana studied Buddhist studies at SOAS (MA 2023–2024) and the University of Oxford (MPhil 2024). He became Founding President and Managing Trustee of the Oxford Buddhist Society in 2023.

Wai-lun Tam specializes in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara, held a post at Hong Kong Polytechnic University, and became professor at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Walenty Skorochód Majewski was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Collegium Nobilium, where he taught in 1785. In 1808, he was placed in charge of the Central Archives of Historical Records.

Walpola Rahula studied at Ceylon, Calcutta, and the Sorbonne under Paul Demiéville. A scholar of Buddhist studies and history, he served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura and Professor of History and Religions at Northwestern University.

Walter A. Fairservis, Jr. was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Chicago, Columbia, and Harvard. He held curatorial posts at the American Museum of Natural History, directed the Burke Museum, and was a professor at Vassar College.
Walter Anthony Cook was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Woodstock College and Georgetown University, where he served as Professor of Linguistics from around 1966 to 1993.

Walter Bruno Henning studied Iranian studies and linguistics at Göttingen under Friedrich Carl Andreas. He held posts at the Prussian Academy of Sciences, SOAS University of London (1936–1961), and the University of California, Berkeley (1961–1967).
Walter Clawiter was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD under Ernst Waldschmidt at the University of Göttingen in 1958 and subsequently held a post there.

Walter Couvreur was a linguist and Indologist who studied at KU Leuven under Albert Joseph Carnoy and at Göttingen under Emil Sieg. After researching at the NFSR, he served as Professor of IE Linguistics at Ghent University from 1949.
Walter Denecke was an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg in 1923, having studied under Hermann Jacobi and Walther Schubring.

Walter Elliot studied at the East India Company College and the College of Fort St. George. Active in Indology, linguistics, and archaeology, he was Private Secretary to Lord Elphinstone and served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Madras (1859–1860).

Walter Emile van Wijk was an Indologist and historian who earned his doctorate at Leiden University. He served as Privatdozent at Leiden, Director of Museon (1933–1938), and Director at Cité Internationale Universitaire de Paris (1938–1953).

Walter Eugene Clark was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Harvard, Berlin under Richard Pischel, and Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He taught at the University of Chicago before serving as Wales Professor of Sanskrit at Harvard (1927–1950).
